evidence.exact_quote: Subagent selection controls must use registry-backed selection and validation, including overrides, disabled lists, and required lists; subagent names must not be hardcoded and invalid override, disabled, or required entries must be rejected or filtered as specified by the source span.

Subagent execution must resolve platform and model for the tier, fetch coordination context, and register each selected agent in coordination state with identity, platform, node, worktree, file, operation, and timestamp fields before execution.

Subagent execution preserves both configured parallel and sequential lifecycle paths, including async dispatch, join_all result propagation, sequential execute_subagent calls, and post-execution unregister_agent cleanup.

Single-subagent execution builds the invocation, marks the agent operation active, executes through the platform runner with the selected subagent, extracts file operations from output, updates coordination files, and returns SubagentOutput.

Platform-specific subagent invocation formatting must be delegated to platform_specs::get_subagent_invocation_format, then filled with subagent, task, context, and coordination values without local platform match statements or duplicated format strings.

Subagent output evidence includes extracting file operations from findings file fields and from task_report, downstream_context, or findings text so coordination state can record files touched by a subagent.

items.impact: A dispatch or update error can leave agents permanently registered or active, parallel failures can produce inconsistent cleanup, and unescaped invocation values can alter provider commands. Text-derived file paths can create false coordination conflicts, expose sensitive paths, or misreport mutation scope.
items.statement: Registry use and DRY formatting are explicit, but required-versus-disabled conflict resolution, empty selection behavior, registration idempotency, finally-style unregister semantics, cancellation and partial-result handling, placeholder escaping, output path normalization, and structured-over-text precedence are not defined.
items.title: Subagent execution lifecycle can leak coordination state and trust parsed output

evidence.exact_quote: Subagent orchestration failure handling preserves fallbacks and best-effort behavior: selection failures warn and fall back or skip, coordination registration/update failures warn and continue, and subagent execution failures log errors and continue with the next subagent or fail a critical tier.

Orchestrator consumes the Executor-owned execution_unit_context contract and schema for worker spawn, recovery, remediation, coordination, and related runtime inspection anchors; TierContext and tier_id remain derived or compatibility-only selection/decomposition vocabulary and are never canonical runtime state.
UI inspection anchors to execution_unit_context as a consumer of canonical runtime context rather than to TierContext or tier_id runtime canon.

Each execution_unit_context receives a lane-managed worktree lease; package or seam reuse is allowed only when lineage matches the lane assignment and no contamination guard is active, while contaminated worktrees are quarantined and cleanup waits for archive, receipt, and recovery checks instead of age alone.

scm_lineage_snapshot is a projector-owned Orchestrator consumer snapshot assembled from canonical runtime, storage, and Source Control records and preserving the full listed field set, including project/repo/worktree identity, worktree state, commit/compare fields, owner lineage, safe-point fields, active git operation, last commit summary, and pr_ref.

Progress surfaces, graph/detail views, History rows, blocked cards, and run receipts consume scm_lineage_snapshot projection data for explicit worktree status values while mutation authority, safe-point restore rules, compare target calculation, and persisted SCM evidence remain with their owner docs.

items.impact: Best-effort continuation can conceal loss of coordination, and an undefined criticality rule can produce inconsistent stop behavior. Lease races or crash recovery can allow reuse of contaminated worktrees, while stale or sensitive SCM snapshots can mislead users about mutation safety and expose local paths or repository details.
items.statement: Shared context ownership and secret exclusions are explicit, but fallback versus skip policy, criticality, degraded coordination visibility, lease acquire/renew/release and crash recovery, snapshot version/freshness/atomicity, UI redaction, and stale/unknown status presentation remain unspecified.
items.title: Failure continuation, worktree leases, and SCM projections lack safe degraded states

items.statement: The retirement list has no successor-field mapping or sunset oracle; timeout handling omits clock basis, clamp formula, cancellation acknowledgement, late-response and usage-write races, and shell teardown proof; benefit and Phase 1-3 backlog units provide lists of intent rather than falsifiable completion criteria aligned to the newer graph ontology.
items.title: Retirement, timeout supervision, and implementation backlogs lack closure criteria

evidence.exact_quote: The implementation-phase source backlog preserves Phase 4 Error Pattern Detection work: detecting error patterns from iteration outputs, automatically invoking debugger/security-auditor/etc., and pattern-based subagent selection.

Phase 5 verification preserves multi-language selection checks plus provider connectivity smoke tests, subagent-invocation integration tests, and plan mode CLI verification as environment-gated or manual verification families.

Provider connectivity smoke tests validate invocation paths and basic behavior for CLI-bridged Cursor and Claude Code, Server-bridged OpenCode, and Direct providers Codex, GitHub Copilot, and Gemini through minimal non-destructive prompts, transport prerequisites, and explicit environment gates.

The provider probe matrix preserves per-platform smoke commands and assertions: Cursor and Claude CLI probes, OpenCode server handshake, Direct-provider Codex/Copilot/Gemini API probes, exit-success checks, non-empty output, and parseable JSON or expected response shape.

Provider smoke tests preserve the source example location and Cursor test sketch, including ignored test attributes, cargo ignored runner guidance, binary lookup for agent or cursor-agent, and SMOKE_OK output-shape checks.

Subagent-invocation integration tests must verify the exact command line built by the orchestrator for tier and subagent execution, use the same builder/code path instead of duplicating logic, and remain environment-gated with optional evidence logs.

The subagent invocation test matrix preserves the integration test file/name list and summary table expectations for platform CLI smoke, subagent-invocation integration, and plan mode CLI verification.

items.impact: Untrusted iteration output can trigger privileged or costly workers without an authority gate, and environment-gated probes can send repository or credential-adjacent data externally, hang, or leave sensitive evidence. Exit code and output shape alone can pass semantically wrong provider behavior, while same-builder command tests can be tautological and miss quoting attacks.
items.statement: Automatic error-pattern invocation lacks confidence, authorization, deduplication, and false-positive rules; provider verification lacks required environment coverage, timeout/retry and credential controls, prompt/data minimization, response-semantic assertions, evidence redaction/retention, adversarial quoting cases, and exact matrix pass/fail criteria.
items.title: Automatic specialist invocation and provider probes lack safety and semantic proof
